text: You've already covered the general idea of multi-factor authentication elsewhere in this catalog. Entra ID can enforce that baseline through Security defaults — every sign-in, every user, MFA required, no exceptions. Simple and effective, but blunt: it treats a sign-in from the office on a company laptop exactly the same as one from an unrecognized device halfway around the world. Conditional Access is Entra ID's answer to that bluntness.

A Conditional Access policy is a rule with two parts: conditions, the signals it evaluates about a sign-in, and controls, what happens if those conditions are met. If this is true about the sign-in attempt, then require this before letting it through. Policies live under Entra ID and require an Entra ID P1 license, one of the premium features that license unlocks, which is exactly why it came up back in Lesson 6.

A policy can check who is signing in — a specific user or one of those security groups from Lesson 6 — where the sign-in is coming from, using a named location like the corporate IP range, what device is being used, whether it's a known compliant device or an unmanaged one, and which application is being accessed.

Once the conditions match, a policy applies one or more controls: require MFA, require a compliant device, require a password change, or block access outright. Controls can combine — require both MFA and a compliant device for a particularly sensitive application, for instance.

The real payoff is adaptive, risk-based enforcement instead of one blunt rule for everyone. Basic MFA prompts every single sign-in. Conditional Access lets a user inside the corporate network on a known device skip that extra prompt, while the same user signing in from an unfamiliar device or location gets stopped for MFA. It doesn't turn MFA off for anyone — it decides when to actually demand it.

A Finance analyst working from the office signs in with just a password, since the location condition isn't met. The same analyst signing in from a coffee shop gets an MFA prompt before Entra ID lets them through — one policy, two outcomes, driven by the signal that changed.
